Bill.BriefDescription: Concerning the education of surgical technologists.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the education of surgical technologists;amending RCW 18.215.020; adding new sections to chapter 18.215 RCW;creating a new section; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.215.020 and 1999 c 335 s 3 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: No person may represent oneself as a surgical technologist by useof any title or description, or perform the functions of a surgicaltechnologist, without being registered by the department under theprovisions of this chapter.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 18.215 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In order to perform functions in a hospital licensed under chapter70.41 RCW, a registered surgical technologist must first submitevidence of any one of the following to the department in a manneracceptable to the secretary: (1) Successful completion of a nationally and programmaticallyaccredited surgical technology program; p. 1 SHB 1555 (2) Successful completion of a surgical technology program offeredby the United States armed forces; or (3) Performance of surgical technology functions in a hospital fora period of one year in the five years immediately preceding January 1,2015.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 18.215 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Nothing in this chapter prohibits or affects: (1) A person licensed under this title acting within his or herscope of practice; (2) A person performing functions in the discharge of officialduties on behalf of the United States government including, but notlimited to, the armed forces, coast guard, public health service,veterans' bureau, or bureau of Indian affairs; or (3) A person completing the clinical portion of a surgicaltechnology education program.
The department of health shall adopt rulesnecessary to implement this act.
Sections 1 through 3 of this act take effectAugust 1, 2014.
